comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 History EER and student curriculum describe the 180 EC full-time Dutch-taught BA. The History track and Foundations of Europe are selected by official order. The major includes 60 EC of foundational courses, a 30 EC depth package, 15 EC of track-specific writing and historical foundations, and a 15 EC thesis. The four package courses and the writing and historical foundations courses require 45 EC at introductory level. Thesis entry requires 30 EC at advanced level and a qualifying Seminar A. The 60 EC profiling space includes a 30 EC coherent package and 30 EC of free electives. At least 15 EC of the profiling space must be at level 2 or 3.
components: Introduction to History as a Discipline (GE1V14001)
The 30 EC Foundations of Europe package starts here. Entry to its four courses requires 45 EC at introductory level.
Research Seminar A: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21001)
Research Seminar B: Foundations of Europe (GE3V21015)
The writing course and Foundations of History also require 45 EC at introductory level.
Students must earn at least 30 EC at advanced level and complete a qualifying Research Seminar A before starting the 15 EC thesis.
Choose a minor or approved study abroad. Across the full 60 EC of electives, at least 15 EC must be at level 2 or 3.
Options include individual courses, a second minor or an internship of up to 15 EC.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized Geschiedenis target does not select between the two formal tracks or among their seven depth packages. The adopted 2026-2027 OER lists Track Geschiedenis before Internationale betrekkingen in historisch perspectief and lists De fundamenten van Europa first within Track Geschiedenis. That package is therefore selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The 60-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

candidates.label: International relations, conflict and global power
Societal challenges, inequality and economic history

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic historical identity, research methods and present-day relevance and responds most directly to the selected Foundations of Europe package through history, archaeology, art, religion, identity and material culture. Two further official, evidence-backed and feasible directions remain: International Relations in Historical Perspective, focused on world order, conflict and security; and Societal Challenges, focused on inequality, capitalism and prosperity. History education is assessed but rejected because UCR does not provide the sequenced pedagogy, school placement or teaching qualification implied by that later outcome. The three included curricula share the complete six-course UCR History sequence but diverge substantially in their adjacent disciplinary courses. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: History, Europe & cultural identity
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines every available UCR History course with archaeology, art history, sociology, heritage, literature, media and historical writing. It is the closest feasible response to the officially selected Foundations of Europe package's emphasis on power, religion, cities and cultural identity, without implying that UCR offers a full History major.
alternatives.concept: Study historical change through history, archaeology, art and heritage. Examine how power, religion and cultural identity shape societies and how historians interpret written, material and visual sources.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 8 level-300 courses. Current offerings and earlier prerequisites were verified.

alternatives.label: History, international relations & conflict
alternatives.labelReason: The route retains all six UCR History courses while concentrating its adjacent work in comparative politics, international relations, conflict, international and EU law, institutions and global governance. The label states the organising fields without claiming a dedicated diplomatic-history degree.
alternatives.concept: Study the history of empires and warfare alongside international relations, law and comparative politics. Examine how conflict, institutions and global power shape societies over time.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces most of its archaeology, art, heritage, literature and media work with law, comparative politics, international relations, EU politics and Peace & Conflict. The organising question moves from European cultural identity and historical representation to international order, institutions, conflict and power.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 7 level-300 courses. Current offerings and earlier prerequisites were verified.

alternatives.label: History, inequality & political economy
alternatives.labelReason: The route retains the complete available UCR History sequence and adds economics, sociology, political institutions, quantitative and qualitative methods, organisations and public communication. It responds to the official Societal Challenges package and its interests in inequality, capitalism, crises and uneven prosperity.
alternatives.concept: Study historical patterns of inequality through histories of empire, gender and modern society. Use economics, sociology and research methods to examine institutions, economic change and the distribution of resources.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes its archaeology, art, heritage, literature and media concentration and adds economics, econometrics, quantitative methods, political institutions and organisational psychology. Its organising logic is inequality, capitalism, crises and political economy rather than cultural identity and public memory.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 7 level-300 courses. Current offerings and earlier prerequisites were verified.

blocks: Historical periods, comparison & selected Foundations of Europe route
UCR Modern History covers modernity, imperialism, war and decolonisation. Utrecht provides a dedicated contemporary history survey.
UCR History of Empires studies power, legitimacy and identity across empires. Utrecht concentrates on the foundations of Europe and the role of religion.
UCR World Archaeology uses material sources to interpret ancient societies across regions. Utrecht approaches the ancient world through historical study.
UCR studies Renaissance Italy and Mediterranean exchange through art and material culture. Utrecht surveys a broader span of early modern and modern history.
Both develop research questions, evaluate historical sources and write an argument. UCR’s course studies the American Century, while Utrecht’s seminar is part of the Foundations of Europe package.
UCR has no scheduled course providing the dedicated medieval-history breadth and weight of Utrecht's compulsory course.
Historical methods, data, writing & independent inquiry
UCR introduces statistical analysis and research design. Utrecht applies data to historical questions.
Both develop systematic inquiry and source interpretation. UCR studies qualitative social research, while Utrecht teaches historical research.
UCR examines how scholars interpret and write the history of art. Utrecht introduces history as a wider discipline.
No second scheduled UCR course reproduces Utrecht's full compulsory historical-research-laboratory sequence.
UCR courses provide philosophical and social context, but no scheduled course is a dedicated foundations-of-history requirement at Utrecht's specified scope.
Utrecht's 30-EC minor or approved study-abroad package is genuine open profiling space; no single content is invented or equated to one UCR course.

Utrecht's remaining 30 EC is genuine free space, potentially including an internship; UCR choice is distributed across the liberal-arts curriculum and no one scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: Utrecht requires a chronological history sequence, dedicated research labs, a four-course depth package and an individual thesis. UCR combines history with methods and related disciplines. Its options offer different ways to study the past, with less sustained training in medieval history and historical research.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s History bachelor studies societies from antiquity to the present and teaches students to ask historical questions and evaluate evidence. This example follows the Foundations of Europe package.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options share history courses and differ in their emphasis on cultural identity, international relations, or inequality and political economy. Utrecht requires a continuous history curriculum and a 15 EC thesis.
